means:
Lacking the competence, energy, or responsibility to get anything done — useless and unreliable in one word.

The contempt is dismissive rather than angry. A villain is never called feckless; a wastrel is. It brands a whole character, not a single failure: the person who means well, promises much, and year after year delivers nothing. Its natural targets are layabouts, absentee fathers and idle heirs, and it carries a faint Scots–British sneer.
trap:
⚠️ **feckless ≠ reckless.**
- **reckless** = acts *too much*, without care for consequences
- **feckless** = never gets round to acting at all

The reckless one totals the car; the feckless one never got round to buying one.
trick_line: **Feck** is *effect* with the front bitten off — so *feckless* is literally **effect-less**.
trick_unpack: He isn't harmful, he's just a person whose efforts never produce any effect.
sentences: A **feckless** heir, he spent thirty years and most of the estate discovering that he had no talent for anything.
Don't put him on the rota — he's **feckless**; he'll say yes and then just not show up.
in_the_wild: British tabloids and welfare debates run on the phrase **\"feckless fathers\"** — men who won't work and won't pay. If you've seen the word in print, it was probably in that collocation.
one_line: Useless and irresponsible; incapable of getting anything done.
